history: Beijing has 3,000+ years of city history and 870+ years as a capital. From the Yan state's Ji city, through the Jin Zhongdu and the world-famous Yuan Dadu, to the Forbidden City and Temple of Heaven of Ming and Qing — Liang Sicheng called it 'an incomparable masterpiece of urban planning'. The Great Wall winds over its northern hills. Since 1949 it has been China's capital — its political, cultural, international and sci-tech center. Seven World Heritage sites (Forbidden City, Temple of Heaven, Summer Palace, Zhoukoudian, Ming Tombs, Great Wall, Grand Canal) sit here, and the Central Axis joined the World Heritage List in 2024.
importance: Capital of China · National central city · Among the richest cities in World Heritage sites
unis: Grown from the Boxer Indemnity study-abroad school; China's top engineering and research university.
From the Imperial University of Peking — China's first national comprehensive university, heart of the New Culture Movement.
Grew from Shaanbei Public School; a leader in humanities and social sciences.
China's first normal university — 'learn to be a teacher, act as a model'.
New China's first aviation and aerospace university; built the country's first light passenger plane.
Born in Yan'an — the first science and engineering university founded by the CPC.
From the agriculture school of the Imperial University; No.1 in agricultural science.
Comprehensive university famous for ethnic studies, with a rich ethnology museum.
Teaches more languages than any other Chinese school — 'cradle of the Republic's diplomats'.
Top university of international economics and trade.
New China's first finance school — the 'Whampoa of finance'.
Strong in information technology; cradle of China's telecom talent.
From the Railway Management School — birthplace of China's railway management education.
Formed from six mining and metallurgy departments; leads in metallurgy and materials.
High-level university known for chemical engineering and materials science.
Top in forestry and landscape architecture — 'know mountains and water, grow trees and people'.
Among the first TCM universities of New China.
Leader in electric power — the 'Whampoa Military Academy' of the power industry.
A center of legal education — 'virtue, law, inquiry, fairness'.
Famous media university — cradle of CCTV anchors.
National center of music education, creation and research.
From the first national art school in Chinese history.
New China's first PE university; home of Olympic champions.
Beijing's key municipal university serving city development.
An important base for Beijing's basic-education teachers.
Strong clinical medicine with several famous teaching hospitals.
Known for business, light industry and food science.

foods: Roast duck with fruitwood, skin crispy red; carved in 108 slices, wrapped in pancakes with scallion and sweet sauce — a state-banquet taste.
Fried yellow soybean sauce noodles with eight toppings — old Beijing's home-style No.1 dish.
Mung-bean fermented drink with crispy rings — real old Beijingers love it sour.
Copper pot on charcoal, clear broth; hand-cut lamb swished 'seven up eight down', dipped in sesame sauce.
Hawthorn on a stick in crystal sugar — the classic winter alley snack, sweet and sour.
Glutinous-rice roll with bean paste in soybean flour — named after donkeys rolling in yellow dust.
Thirteen cuts of beef tripe, swished seconds in boiling water — springy, with sesame sauce.
Pork offal stewed with baked wheat cakes — from palace kitchen to street favorite.
Pea-flour pudding, smooth as jade, melts in the mouth — Empress Dowager Cixi's favorite sweet.
Beef and lamb grilled on an iron tray with fruitwood aroma — eaten standing for full flavor.
scenes: Home of 24 Ming and Qing emperors — the world's largest wooden palace complex, 9,371 rooms, World Heritage since 1987.
'You are not a hero until you reach the Great Wall' — the finest Ming wall winding along the Jundu ridge.
Where emperors prayed for harvests; the triple blue glazed roof of the Hall of Prayer is Beijing's icon.
Imperial garden museum — Kunming Lake, Longevity Hill and the Seventeen-Arch Bridge, World Heritage since 1998.
One of the world's largest city squares; the morning flag-raising ceremony is solemn and moving.
Hutong district formed in the Yuan era; 800-meter lane with alleys like centipede legs — cafes and snacks.
Imperial garden of five dynasties; the White Dagoba on Jade Islet — the lake in the song 'Let Us Sway Twin Oars'.
Bird's Nest — the woven steel stadium of both the 2008 Summer and 2022 Winter Olympic openings.
Tombs of thirteen Ming emperors with a solemn sacred way, World Heritage since 2003.
Yonghe Temple — the emperor's former residence turned Tibetan Buddhist lamasery, with an 18-meter sandalwood Buddha.
